rationale: The cassette totals 5,340 bp: AAV2 ITRs, the 1,639 bp CAG promoter, a 3,186 bp payload and the 225 bp bGH polyA. That is 640 bp over the 4,700 bp single stranded target and 140 bp over the 5,200 bp hard ceiling, so aav.packaging_limit is the check that must catch it: it is the only check that measures 5' ITR start through 3' ITR end against the band, and above the soft limit its severity is FAIL rather than WARN. A capsid cannot package this genome, so the run would produce truncated species. The case also asserts the remediation field, because section 6.5 requires a FAIL here to name a specific element substitution that would fix it, computed from the part registry. The payload is a length-calibrated tandem concatenation of whole in-frame copies of the real beta-lactamase reading frame of pUC19, GenBank L09137.1 (tests/fixtures/parser/puc19.gb) with one terminal stop codon, assembled only to put the cassette at the exact length this case is about. It is not a real gene and nothing here presents it as one; the defect under test is the length, not the payload.

4,800 bp: 100 bp over the 4,700 bp target and 100 bp under the 4,900 bp soft limit. The verdict must be WARN and not FAIL, because a genome in that band packages with reduced efficiency rather than not at all, and flattening it to FAIL would reject designs that real laboratories run. aav.packaging_limit is the check under test and this case pins the lower boundary of its band, which is the number most likely to drift. The remediation is asserted here too: section 6.5 requires the overage in base pairs, and the engine supplies the substitutions alongside it. The payload is a length-calibrated tandem concatenation of whole in-frame copies of the real beta-lactamase reading frame of pUC19, GenBank L09137.1 (tests/fixtures/parser/puc19.gb) with one terminal stop codon, assembled only to put the cassette at the exact length this case is about. It is not a real gene and nothing here presents it as one; the defect under test is the length, not the payload.

A 3,000 bp cassette that is entirely legal as a single stranded genome, 1,700 bp under the 4,700 bp target, but is declared self complementary. A self complementary genome is an inverted repeat of the cassette, so the capsid has to hold roughly twice the length and the usable capacity halves: 3,000 bp is 600 bp over the 2,400 bp self complementary target and 400 bp over the 2,600 bp hard ceiling. aav.sc_capacity is the check that must catch it, and aav.packaging_limit must NOT fail, because the length is fine for the single stranded modality it is not using. That split is the whole point of the case: it proves the halved band is applied to the right designs and that the failure names the reason. The payload is a length-calibrated tandem concatenation of whole in-frame copies of the real beta-lactamase reading frame of pUC19, GenBank L09137.1 (tests/fixtures/parser/puc19.gb) with one terminal stop codon, assembled only to put the cassette at the exact length this case is about. It is not a real gene and nothing here presents it as one; the defect under test is the length, not the payload.

The 3' ITR element is absent. The ITRs are the only viral sequence a recombinant AAV genome retains and they are required in cis for replication and packaging, so a cassette with one ITR does not become a vector at all. aav.itr_present_both is the check that must catch it, because it is the only one that asks whether both ITRs exist and match the serotype reference. aav.itr_orientation and aav.itr_internal_sites report UNKNOWN rather than PASS, which is correct: with one ITR there is no pair to orient and no interior between two ITRs to scan. Neither may be read as a pass and neither is a FAIL, so this case still has exactly one failure.

elements.name: orf405_bla_segment
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: Both ITR slots carry the left ITR as written, so the two repeats are in tandem rather than inverted. Each ITR on its own matches the AAV2 reference, so aav.itr_present_both passes and cannot catch this: the defect is purely relative orientation. aav.itr_orientation is the check that must catch it, decided from the 20 nt D element, which in a correct inverted pair faces inward from both ends and here faces the same way twice. A tandem pair does not form the hairpin the replication machinery needs, so the genome does not replicate or package.

elements.name: orf405_bla_segment
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

elements.name: AAV2 left ITR placed as the 3' ITR

rationale: The polyA element is removed entirely. Without a polyadenylation signal the transcript is not cleaved or polyadenylated, so it is unstable and poorly exported and the vector expresses almost nothing. aav.required_elements is the check that must catch it, because promoter, coding sequence and polyA are the three elements it exists to confirm. aav.polya_present_functional also fails, and that is a genuine cascade from the one defect rather than a second defect: check 12 asks whether the polyA present is a recognised functional signal, and with no polyA element at all there is nothing for it to recognise, which section 6.4 says is a FAIL and not an UNKNOWN. Both failures name the same missing element, so it is listed in allowed_extra_fail rather than hidden.

elements.name: orf405_bla_segment
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: A 135 bp real fragment of pUC19 occupies the polyA slot. It is the right size for a polyA and it is real DNA, so every structural check passes and aav.required_elements is satisfied by the element being present, but it carries neither AATAAA nor ATTAAA, so it is not a polyadenylation signal. This is the mistake of annotating the wrong fragment as the polyA, which no length or order check can see. aav.polya_present_functional is the only check that reads the sequence for a recognised hexamer, and section 6.4 gives it WARN for an unrecognised signal rather than FAIL, because a functional signal this module does not know is possible and the user is better placed to judge.

elements.name: orf405_bla_segment
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

elements.name: mis-annotated 135 bp fragment
elements.source: pUC19, GenBank L09137.1 (tests/fixtures/parser/puc19.gb) plus strand 1..135, placed in the polyA slot

rationale: Codon 21 of the real reading frame is replaced by TAA, giving a premature in-frame stop while the length, the start codon and the terminal stop all stay correct. The vector would be built, would package and would express a 20 residue fragment instead of the protein, which is the expensive kind of mistake because nothing about the construct looks wrong. aav.cds_integrity is the only check that translates the reading frame, so it is the only one that can catch this, and its message gives the cassette position of the offending codon. The substitution is synthetic and deliberate: the point is the defect, and everything around it is the real frame.

elements.name: orf405 with a premature stop at codon 21
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: One base is removed from the 3' end of the real reading frame, so the coding sequence is 404 bp. The length is not divisible by three, which means the reading frame does not close and the terminal stop codon is no longer in frame. This is the classic one base cloning slip. aav.cds_integrity is the check that must catch it, and it reports both consequences and says how many bases to add or remove. It is a separate case from the premature stop because a single check with several conditions can pass one and fail another, and both conditions are named in section 6.4 check 6.

elements.name: orf405 with one 3' base removed
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: Every required element is present and every sequence is real, but the polyA sits between the promoter and the coding sequence instead of after it. Transcription would terminate and polyadenylate before reaching the transgene, so the cassette expresses nothing. aav.required_elements passes, because presence is all it checks, and the length is unchanged, so aav.element_order is the only check that can catch this: it compares the element roles against the section 6.2 functional order. The Kozak warning that comes with it is a true consequence of the polyA now sitting in front of the start codon, and it is a WARN, so the case still has exactly one failure.

elements.name: orf405_bla_segment
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: A liver-targeted vector driven by the hSyn1 promoter, which is neuron specific. The cassette is 2,437 bp, structurally perfect and comfortably inside the packaging band, so no length or structural check sees anything: this is precisely the design error section 6.2 says no length check will catch. The transgene would simply not be expressed in hepatocytes. aav.promoter_tissue_match is the check that must catch it, comparing the part's tissue_specificity annotation with the requested target_tissue, and the severity is WARN because the designer, not the registry, knows the intended cell type. The payload is the complete 861 bp beta-lactamase reading frame of pUC19, GenBank L09137.1 (tests/fixtures/parser/puc19.gb), ATG through TAA, whose native initiation context also warns; that is a WARN, so the case still reports no failure at all, which is the expected outcome.

A 60 bp stretch of the reading frame is duplicated in frame immediately after itself, so the cassette carries a 60 bp direct repeat between the ITRs while the coding sequence stays a clean open reading frame: the duplication is a whole number of codons and adds no stop, so aav.cds_integrity still passes and cannot catch it. Direct repeats above 20 bp recombine during vector production, which deletes the intervening sequence and yields a mixed, partly truncated preparation. aav.internal_repeats is the only check that looks for repeated substrings inside the cassette, so it is the one that must catch it. The duplication is a deliberate synthetic edit to a real frame.

elements.name: orf405 with a 60 bp in-frame duplication
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: An 887 bp cassette: AAV2 ITRs, the 225 bp MeCP2 mini promoter, a 237 bp payload and the 135 bp SV40 polyA, with no WPRE. Everything is structurally correct, the promoter matches the cns_neuron target and the reading frame is clean, so the only thing wrong is that the genome is 1,113 bp below the 2,000 bp floor. Genomes this small package inefficiently and raise the empty capsid fraction, so the titer per production run drops. aav.minimum_genome_size is the only check that looks at the lower end of the band, which makes it the one that must catch it, and it is a WARN because the vector does work, just less well, and the fix is to add stuffer sequence.

elements.name: orf237_bla_segment
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: Both ITRs are present and in the inverted orientation, but the 5' ITR carries 21 transversions, dropping its identity to the AAV2 reference below the 0.95 threshold. The D element is untouched, so aav.itr_orientation still decides inverted correctly and passes, which isolates the defect: this is an ITR that is in the right place and the right orientation and is simply no longer an AAV2 ITR. aav.itr_present_both is the check that must catch it, because it is the one that measures identity against the serotype reference rather than merely counting elements, and that distinction is what makes presence checking useful.

elements.name: degenerate 5' ITR
elements.source: AAV2 left ITR (itr.aav2_itr_left) with 21 transversions introduced for this case

elements.name: orf405_bla_segment
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: The promoter element is removed, so the coding sequence sits directly against the 5' ITR. Nothing drives transcription, so the vector packages and expresses nothing. aav.required_elements is the check that must catch it. Two other checks correctly decline to guess: aav.promoter_tissue_match reports UNKNOWN because there is no promoter annotation to compare with the target tissue, which must never read as a pass. The companion case to aav.bad.no_polya, with the other required element.

elements.name: orf405_bla_segment
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: Twelve adenines are inserted in frame into the reading frame, which is four lysine codons, so the open reading frame stays clean and aav.cds_integrity passes. A run of twelve identical bases is over the 8 bp threshold: long homopolymers cause polymerase slippage during synthesis and during vector replication, so the ordered DNA and the packaged genome can both differ from the design. aav.homopolymer_runs is the only check that measures single base runs, so it is the one that must catch it. The insertion is a deliberate synthetic edit to a real frame, chosen to be in frame precisely so that no other check can fire.

elements.name: orf405 with a 12 base adenine run inserted in frame
elements.source: pUC19 beta-lactamase open reading frame, GenBank L09137.1 minus strand

rationale: The first 21 bases of the AAV2 ITR are inserted in frame into the payload, so a copy of an ITR motif sits inside the cassette as well as at both ends. The ITRs themselves are correct and correctly oriented, and the reading frame survives because the insertion is a whole number of codons that adds no stop. An internal ITR motif gives the replication machinery a third place to resolve, which produces snapback and truncated genomes during production. aav.itr_internal_sites is the check that exists for exactly this and it is the only one that compares the interior against the serotype ITR reference on both strands. The insertion is a deliberate synthetic edit.
